name: no-per-layer-norm-operand-discovery
kind: DISCOVERY — the deliverable is a CLASSIFICATION, not a verdict delta. Nothing is implemented in this wave, and a GREEN count is not how it is scored.
baseline: wave 13 (semantics 12): GREEN 41 / AMBER 3 / RED 65 / BUG 0 / silent drops 0 / blockers 1044
the_population: 12 rows whose execution surface refuses with `norm placement (stack carries no per-layer norm operands)` — the largest of the three norm-placement shapes found in the wave-11 rerank, and the one deliberately left until last because premature implementation was the risk.
the_method_and_its_constraint: Class derived from THREE sources per row and never from a filename or an absence: (1) the reference forward implementation where one exists; (2) the ACTUAL tensor inventory, read from each checkpoint's safetensors header over HTTP range requests rather than assumed; (3) the config. Where no reference exists, that is recorded as a fact about the evidence rather than papered over.
the_headline: It is NOT one problem. Four families, three distinct causes, and none of the twelve rows is legitimately normless — every one of them HAS per-layer norms. The refusal was reading the absence of four specific SPELLINGS as the absence of an operator.

classification.actual_architecture_fact: It has two per-layer norms and they are spelled `operator_norm` and `ffn_norm`. `Lfm2DecoderLayer.forward` is `residual = h; h = mixer(operator_norm(h)); h = h + residual; h = h + feed_forward(ffn_norm(h))` — a standard two-norm PRE-only stack, structurally identical to what `NormPlacement::PreOnly` already executes. The mixer is attention on the layers named in `full_attn_idxs` and a short conv elsewhere. The config also spells its epsilon `norm_eps` (with a separate `block_norm_eps`), not `rms_norm_eps`.
classification.next_action: Role-table entries for `operator_norm` -> PreAttentionNorm and `ffn_norm` -> PreFfnNorm, plus the `norm_eps` config spelling. No new placement and no new operator: the shape is one this build already runs.

classification.family: nemotron_h (Nemotron-3 Nano-4B / Nano-30B-A3B / Super-120B / Ultra-550B, Nemotron-3.5 Lightning)
classification.actual_architecture_fact: One norm per BLOCK — `backbone.layers.N.norm.weight` (42 of them on Nano-4B) — plus the Mamba2 mixer's own gated norm `backbone.layers.N.mixer.norm.weight` (21) and a final `backbone.norm_f.weight`. `NemotronHBlock`'s own docstring: 'Each block applies pre-normalization followed by the mixer, then adds a residual connection.' The estate is the mamba_ssm lineage's (`backbone.` / `mixer.`), and the config declares its schedule as `hybrid_override_pattern` ('M-M-M-MM-...') with `layer_norm_epsilon` beside `rms_norm_eps`.
classification.classification: C for the spelling, D for the topology — and the second is the load-bearing half
classification.why_it_is_not_only_a_dialect: A Nemotron-H 'layer' is ONE block carrying ONE mixer — Mamba, attention, MLP or MoE — with a single norm and a single residual add. VINDEX3's layer model is an attention-class operator PAIRED with an FFN. `NormPlacement::PreMixer` already describes one-norm-one-operator for a pure-SSM stack; what is absent is that shape with HETEROGENEOUS block types in one stack. Mapping the names without the topology would pair blocks that the reference never pairs.
classification.next_action: Forecast the block-topology semantic first, as its own wave. The naming is a prerequisite, not the fix.

classification.actual_architecture_fact: It has `layers.N.attn_norm.weight` and `layers.N.ffn_norm.weight`, 43 of each — the same two-norm shape under a third spelling, with no `model.` prefix at all. But the estate ALSO carries `layers.N.hc_attn_scale`, `layers.N.hc_ffn_scale` and `hc_head_scale`: hyper-connections, a residual topology in which the sublayer output is combined through learned per-site scales rather than added plainly.
classification.classification: C for the norms, D for the residual topology
classification.next_action: The dialect entries are cheap and would let the surface build — and that is exactly the trap. Building the surface without hyper-connections would produce a component whose residual arithmetic is wrong while every declaration has a home. Hyper-connections must be represented (or explicitly refused) BEFORE the norms are mapped, or this row goes GREEN and cannot execute.
classification.no_reference_available: transformers 5.5.0 ships no `deepseek_v4` modeling code, so the forward is not readable here. That is a fact about the evidence: the classification above rests on the tensor estate and the config, and the hyper-connection semantics would need the checkpoint's own remote code before anything is implemented.

classification.actual_architecture_fact: There is NO plain per-layer norm at all. The only per-layer norms are INSIDE hyper-connection modules — `layers.N.attn_hyper_connection.hc_norm.weight` and `layers.N.mlp_hyper_connection.hc_norm.weight`, 48 of each — beside a stack-level `hyper_connection_mixer.hc_norm`, per-layer-embedding norms (`ple.norm_conv`, `ple.norm_key`, `ple.norm_query`) and an MTP head with its own `pre_fc_norm_*` pair.
classification.classification: D — execution semantic genuinely absent (with a B flavour: the norm IS represented, through another object)
classification.why_it_is_the_cleanest_D: The other three rows have a norm that a role-table entry could bind. This one's norm is a COMPONENT of a mechanism this schema does not have. Binding `hc_norm` to a pre-attention norm role would not be a dialect mapping; it would be asserting a residual topology the checkpoint does not use.
classification.next_action: Nothing until hyper-connections are represented. This row is the right witness for that semantic, and it is already blocked on 36 concepts, so it is a poor early target.

what_this_says_about_the_remaining_work: The wave-11 rerank counted this population as one cluster of 12 rows and 13-36 blockers each. It is four families and three causes, and the cheap half (4 LFM2 rows, a pure naming dialect over a placement this build already executes) is separable from the expensive half (hyper-connections on 3 rows, heterogeneous block topology on 5). That is the pattern the earlier sweeps kept finding: one compatibility cluster hiding distinct causal semantics — see the wave-10 rerank, where `architecture_identity` looked causal and was not.
the_follow_up_forecasts_to_freeze_after_: LFM2 dialect: role-table entries for `operator_norm`/`ffn_norm` and the `norm_eps` config spelling. Predict per row which of the remaining 13-24 blockers actually clear — the norms are one idea among several on these rows (conv geometry, `full_attn_idxs`, block sizing), so the surface building is NOT the same as the row clearing.
Nemotron-H block topology: a stack whose layers are single heterogeneous blocks. Forecast the SCHEMA change, and expect it to reveal rather than retire — these rows carry 20-29 blockers each.

Hyper-connections: represent or explicitly refuse, with DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as the witnesses. Until then, the LFM2 and Nemotron dialect work must not be allowed to make a hyper-connection row admissible.
the_trap_this_wave_exists_to_avoid: Three of the four families would have their surface BUILD from role-table entries alone, because their norms are really there under other names. Two of those three also carry a residual topology this schema cannot express. Adding the names first would move rows toward GREEN while leaving their arithmetic wrong — the same shape as wave 13's skipped FFN, which the sweep could not see and only a real-checkpoint witness caught.
